Ana: Heads-up — Grafana token-level dashboard (p50/p95/p99 TTFT) in eu-west showing brief p99 spikes after last runtime deploy. Might be rollup change or sampling noise. Anyone seeing this?
Jeff: Noted. Can you paste a link to the dash + the panel? I can check the PromQL and the histogram rollup.
Ana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/token-latency?orgId=1&panelId=7
Panel query uses histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard, model_version))
Spikes look correlated with small bursts of tokens/sec.
Maria: I saw related egress retries from eu-west nodes around the same windows. Logs show transient connection resets to kvcache. Could be network noise causing tail latency.
Raj: Two quick callouts: - histogram_quantile is sensitive to bucket boundaries + aggregation order; - if rollup changed to sum(rate(...)) across shards before quantile, it can create artificial tail changes. We should check if aggregation was moved earlier in the pipeline last week.
Jeff: Agree. Also sampling density matters. If tokens/sec per-shard drops, the rate() becomes noisier. Recommend adding an explicit tokens/sec panel and gating p99 alert with token volume threshold.
sre-bot: Alert: TTFT_p99_eu-west > 1.2s fired (rule/ttft_p99_eu-west) at 2067894340
grafana-bot: Snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/snapshot/xyz (expires in 7d)
Ana: PromQL I'm experimenting with to reduce noise:
```
sum by(shard, model_version) (
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le, shard, model_version))
)
```
But maybe better to compute quantile per-shard then rollup with max() not sum().
Raj: Exactly — do quantile per shard then take percentile across shards or max. sum() mixes distributions badly. Example:
```
max by(model_version) (
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le, shard, model_version))
)
```
Jeff: If we take max across shards we'll get noisy alerts from one noisy machine. Maybe combine with tokens/sec gating: (tokens_per_shard > 50) and (ttft_p99 > 1s).
Maria: Agreed. Also we should make sure tokens/sec is measured as a per-shard, per-model timeseries so we can join in alerts without expensive instant joins.
Jeff: PromQL for tokens/sec per shard:
```
sum by(shard, model_version) (rate(tokens_processed_total[1m]))
```
Then use a recording rule to downsample and use that in alerts to avoid high query cost.
Ana: Recording rule + precomputed per-shard quantiles sounds right. Also propose: change alert to trigger only if p99 > baseline * 1.15 AND tokens/sec > X for 10m. Baseline can be 95th percentile over last 7d.
Raj: We should avoid expensive histogram_quantile over wide time windows in ad-hoc panels. For dashboards use precomputed timeseries from aggregation pipeline (metrics-aggregator).
Jeff: I'll open a PR for recording rules + alert tweak. Assigning to @jeff and @ana. ETA today for dashboard patch, tomorrow for alert change.
Ana: Thanks. Also add a tokens/sec heatmap per region/model_version so we can correlate demand vs tail.
deploy-bot: Deploy v2-runtime-prod completed at 2067894300 by ci/cd (sha: d4f2b3)
Maria: I'll check kvcache logs and open SR for network team if we see repeated resets.
Jeff: :thumbsup: I'll wire recording rules and create a minimal dashboard variant 'token-observability-sane-rollup' in staging.
Ana: :thumbsup: thanks everyone.
